gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Pipe-cleaner strokes of constant width give Tektur its look, while Noto Sans Gurmukhi trails with outward-flaring terminals and low ascenders. Tektur earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Laser-cut and unwavering: that's Tektur. Noto Sans Hanunoo takes over with lowercase that fills most of its height and open terminals, so the two hand off to each other smoothly.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aram: Tektur bends its strokes like pipe cleaners, one width throughout, with wide openings on every curve. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic brings the approachable side, its c ends parting like pincers.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian reads wide and clean, with big open eyes and a deep middle band, beneath headings in Tektur. Across a full page, that deep band keeps lines easy on the eye.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Strokes that never thin or thicken give Tektur its bent-wire look. Noto Sans Khojki, with wide exits and a large eye on every e, lets running text glide past without strain.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kr: A drafting-pen outline quality, one constant nib width, gives Tektur its look, while Noto Sans KR stays generous with open curves. Precise drafting above, big-bodied lowercase with stubby ascenders below.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lao: Expressive from the first letter, Tektur moves its stems and arcs in lockstep, while Noto Sans Lao pushes its x-height high. One makes statements; the other keeps text moving.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu sits quietly, its ascenders just shy of the x-height line. Beside the pipe-cleaner letterforms of Tektur, it feels restrained, like a level voice after a loud one.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Wire-bent s curves that never thin at the spine give Tektur its unmistakable look. And Noto Sans Lydian, with capitals barely above its lowercase, supplies a quiet, approachable counterweight.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Distinctive, with one stroke width running through the whole alphabet, Tektur looks bent from wire. Noto Sans Malayalam settles into a dense middle band with generous bends in its s, a gentle foil for it.
